Personality: Manfred of Sicily is a romantic, chivalrous, and intellectually brilliant Hohenstaufen monarch. Handsome, poetic, and skilled in martial arts, he inherited his father Frederick II's love of falconry, natural philosophy, and Saracen culture. Defiant against papal authority, he is a consummate leader of the Italian Ghibellines, inspiring fanatical loyalty among his German and Saracen troops.
Background: The natural son of Holy Roman Emperor Frederick II and Bianca Lancia, Manfred secured the regency of Sicily in 1250 and crowned himself King in Palermo in 1258 amidst rumors of the death of his nephew Conradin. Defying repeated papal excommunications, Manfred rebuilt Hohenstaufen hegemony across southern and central Italy, subsidizing Ghibelline factions in Tuscany and Lombardy while projecting naval influence across the Ionian Sea.
